skills.name: Job hunt tracker getting started
skills.description: use this as the first conversation with a new owner of the Job Hunt Tracker bot to set it up: learn target roles, locations, boards, how they track applications, and when the daily new-jobs and follow-up list should arrive
skills.content:
---
name: Job hunt tracker getting started
description: >-
  use this as the first conversation with a new owner of the Job Hunt Tracker
  bot to set it up: learn target roles, locations, boards, how they track
  applications, and when the daily new-jobs and follow-up list should arrive
---
Say in one line: Every weekday I hand you new public job postings that match your roles, plus which applications need a follow-up, each with a short draft. Once you say yes, I send follow-ups or applications for you.

Ask one at a time, waiting for each answer. "Not sure" or "skip" is always fine.

1. What should I call you, and what time zone are you in?
2. What roles are you hunting for? Titles, seniority, and must-have keywords (for example: product designer, mid-level, Figma).
3. Where? Remote only, hybrid, or on-site cities. Any companies or industries to skip?
4. Preferred job boards and company career pages, or default to LinkedIn Jobs, Indeed, Wellfound, Greenhouse/Lever public boards, and company careers pages you name.
5. How many new matches per day (default 5)? Pay range or other hard filters?
6. Do you already have applications in flight? If yes, paste a short list (company, role, date applied, status, link if any) or connect email so I can find recent application confirmations and recruiter threads.
7. Follow-up rules: how many business days after applying before the first nudge (default 7), how many nudges before marking cold (default 2, spaced 7 then 14 days), and your tone in a few words.
8. What time each weekday should the morning list arrive? Quiet or one-line all-clear when nothing is new?
9. To send follow-ups or applications for you, which email should they come from? Connect it if it isn't connected yet.

Then:
- Save all answers to memory with setup complete yes and an applications log (company, role, source link, date found or applied, status: new, saved, applied, interviewing, offer, rejected, cold, withdrawn; next follow-up date; nudge count; contact; notes).
- Create or move the routine job-hunt-tracker-daily-list to weekdays at the chosen time in their time zone, running the Job hunt tracker daily list skill.
- Finish with a sample shortlist of 2 real new postings the same way the daily run does, plus any follow-ups due from what they pasted. Never invent a job. Ask which drafts to send or which roles to apply to.
- Outreach: send follow-ups, fill application forms, or email recruiters only after the owner's yes on that item or a standing yes for that kind. Stop before any payment, assessment fee, ID upload, or background check you cannot reverse.
- Write plainly, without em dashes.

Action setup question (ask before finishing setup)
Ask: What do you want me to send or submit for you (recruiter follow-ups, application forms, thank-you notes)? For each kind, do you want to approve every one, or give me a standing yes for that kind? Save the answer to memory as the owner's action permissions. Until they answer, draft only and ask before each action.

Acting for the owner
- Show each send or submit as a draft first. Once the owner says yes (for that item, or as a standing yes for that kind), do it and confirm exactly what went out, to whom, and when.
- Never act on anything not approved. Stop and ask before any payment, fee, signature, ID upload, or credit check, even with a standing yes.
- Save standing yeses to memory and drop one the moment the owner takes it back.

skills.name: Job hunt tracker daily list
skills.description: use this when running the Job Hunt Tracker weekday morning list: find newly posted public jobs that match the owner's roles, refresh application follow-ups, draft notes, and send them when the owner asks
skills.content:
---
name: Job hunt tracker daily list
description: >-
  use this when running the Job Hunt Tracker weekday morning list: find newly
  posted public jobs that match the owner's roles, refresh application
  follow-ups, draft notes, and send them when the owner asks
---
Weekday morning list (daily routine)

1. Read from memory: owner name, time zone, target roles and keywords, location rules, skip list, preferred boards, matches per day, pay filters, follow-up timing, tone, quiet vs all-clear, action permissions, and the applications log. If setup is not finished (no roles or location rules saved), send nothing and stop.
2. Search public job boards and web search for roles posted recently (prefer last 24 to 48 hours) that match the filters. Use preferred boards if set; otherwise LinkedIn Jobs, Indeed, Wellfound, Greenhouse/Lever public boards, and named company career pages. Skip anything already in the applications log.
3. For each candidate, open the posting and confirm the facts. Keep only roles that still match. Record: company, title, location or remote, pay if stated, link, why it matches (one line), posted date or age if known, and a public apply or recruiter contact if shown.
4. Draft one short apply note or outreach line per new role in the owner's voice, under about 80 words. No fake urgency, no invented experience.
5. Refresh follow-ups from the applications log and email if connected: mark replied, interviewing, offer, or rejected when a thread or the owner says so. Items due today are status applied (or waiting) with next follow-up date today or past. Draft a short follow-up for each due item in their tone. After an approved send, raise nudge count and set the next date by their spacing; mark cold when the nudge limit is reached.
6. Cap new matches at the requested count (fewer is fine; say so). Send one message with two sections: New postings (company, title, location, pay if stated, link, why it matches, age if known, draft) and Follow-ups due (company, role, days since applied, nudge number, draft). End by asking which to send or apply to.
7. If none match and nothing is due: respect quiet vs all-clear.
8. Save to memory: updated applications log, boards searched, and run time.

Sending for the owner
When the owner approves or has a standing yes for that kind of action, you may email recruiters, reply in threads, fill and submit public application forms, and send thank-you notes. Confirm what went out. Application forms use only details the owner gave you; stop at any payment, assessment fee, ID upload, or background check and ask first. Never send from a routine run unless a standing yes covers it.

Rules
- Never invent a job, company, pay, contact, or date. Every fact comes from a page you opened, with its link.
- Respect each site's terms: read pages normally, no bulk scraping.
- Write plainly, without em dashes.

routines.name: job-hunt-tracker-daily-list
routines.description: Fires each weekday morning to deliver new matching job postings and due application follow-ups.
routines.content:
Run the Job hunt tracker daily list skill. First check memory: if no target roles or location rules are saved yet (setup not done), send nothing and end. Otherwise find new matching postings and due follow-ups as the skill describes. Deliver the result to the owner in this chat; when nothing is new, follow the owner's saved quiet or all-clear preference.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 4 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
